lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Fabiola, this is Tanya. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Tanya. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Kind of down this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Zero. I'm not going to lie to you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the late dinners makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walks after dinner. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar is lower in the morning when I walk after dinner.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the late dinners made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Fabiola. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

flags.reason: Participant said she is 'kind of down' and coach did not explore mood or check for hopelessness or depression.
Health advice given without asking permission, with a directive tone ('really helps'), after a stretch of good reflective listening.

score.summary: The coach used strong complex reflections of ambivalence and change talk, and helped Fabiola set a realistic 3-day goal with barrier planning and a clear summary. The coach missed the 'kind of down' mood cue at line 4 and gave unsolicited health advice at line 38.
strengths: Line 22 and 36: reflected ambivalence well and sustained the change talk.
Line 50: concise summary that confirmed the plan with the participant.
Line 48: asked about barriers before closing, which led to a concrete plan (line 49).
coaching_tips: Line 4: when she said 'kind of down,' ask gently about mood (e.g., 'What's been making it feel heavier?') and check how she is coping.
Line 38: ask permission before sharing information (e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared what walks do for blood sugar?').
Set an agenda early (e.g., 'Today I'd like to check in on your walks and how you've been feeling').
